blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights this vision paper from Microsoft researchers that predicts a major shift in machine learning (ML) from consumer-scale applications to enterprise-grade ML (EGML) systems. The paper argues that EGML applications will require stricter data handling, model fairness, privacy, and debuggability compared to current ML systems. The authors emphasize that ML models are software artifacts derived from data, combining software engineering needs (like CI/CD) with data lineage requirements. They predict that in the next decade, millions of ML-infused applications will be built by smaller teams, necessitating robust platforms for training, inference, and governance. The paper identifies three key areas for EGML systems: model development/training, model scoring (inference), and model management/governance, with a bold prediction that ML inference will become deeply integrated into DBMS as a foundational extension of relational algebra. The blog post also introduces Microsoft's Flock reference architecture, which treats ML models as software artifacts and explores in-DBMS inference for performance gains.
paper_title: Cloudy with a high chance of DBMS: a 10-year prediction for enterprise-grade ML
paper_abstract: Machine learning (ML) has proven itself in high-value web applications such as search ranking and is emerging as a powerful tool in a much broader range of enterprise scenarios including voice recognition and conversational understanding for customer support, autotuning for videoconferencing, intelligent feedback loops in large-scale sysops, manufacturing and autonomous vehicle management, complex financial predictions, just to name a few. Meanwhile, as the value of data is increasingly recognized and monetized, concerns about securing valuable data and risks to individual privacy have been growing. Consequently, rigorous data management has emerged as a key requirement in enterprise settings. How will these trends (ML growing popularity, and stricter data governance) intersect? What are the unmet requirements for applying ML in enterprise settings? What are the technical challenges for the DB community to solve? In this paper, we present our vision of how ML and database systems are likely to come together, and early steps we take towards making this vision a reality.
